description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: Archive-driven complexity estimation before item pick
items.intent: Before starting a sprint item, the orchestrator must consult historical archive data to estimate complexity and warn when an item resembles historically difficult work.
items.description: sprints.jsonl captures attempts, lines changed, and duration per completed item. Use this data to estimate complexity for queued items by matching on category and AC/step count. If historical items in the same category averaged more than 2 attempts, log an advisory note. Purely advisory — does not block or change behavior.
steps: Add estimate_complexity function that reads backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl
Group historical items by category; compute average attempts, duration, and lines changed per category
Before pick_item returns, call estimate_complexity with the picked item category and AC count
If estimated attempts exceed 2 or estimated duration exceeds 30 minutes, log_info an advisory complexity hint
Add a complexity column to print_batch_summary showing estimated vs actual attempts
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Before a sprint item starts, an advisory complexity hint is logged when historical data suggests the category is difficult
Items in categories with no historical data show no hint
The batch summary includes estimated vs actual attempts for each item
Complexity estimation does not block or delay sprint execution
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
items.groomingNotes: Priority 'could' is correct — purely advisory, zero blocking behavior. User value: reduces surprise on hard items by surfacing historical difficulty before the sprint starts. The hint must never appear as an error or warning that implies the sprint should be skipped — it is informational only. AC are appropriately scoped. No dependencies. PO note: dependent on the modularization chain completing so that the script is in a stable state before adding new features; consider moving dependsOn to FEAT-059 to enforce this ordering. Batch summary column is secondary to the pre-sprint hint — if implementation time is limited, the hint alone satisfies user value.

items.title: Add module loader infrastructure
items.intent: Establish the lazy-loading mechanism so subsequent items can extract commands to .aishore/lib/*.sh modules without changing any behavior
steps: Add declare -A _LOADED_MODULES and _load_module function after UTILITIES header
Create empty .aishore/lib/ directory
No dispatch changes yet — pure infrastructure
acceptanceCriteria: All existing commands still work identically
_load_module function exists and can source a file from lib/
items.groomingNotes: Steps are clear and mechanical. Infrastructure-only: add declare -A _LOADED_MODULES and _load_module() after the UTILITIES header (line 414), create empty .aishore/lib/ directory. No dispatch changes. AC are testable: bash -n passes, existing commands still work, _load_module exists. No dependencies. Safe to sprint — zero risk of regressions since it's purely additive.

items.title: Extract cmd-diagnose to module
items.intent: First extraction — prove the lazy-load pattern works on the simplest most isolated command (56 lines, zero deps beyond globals)
steps: Create .aishore/lib/cmd-diagnose.sh with cmd_diagnose function
Remove cmd_diagnose from main script
Update main() dispatch to use _load_module cmd-diagnose
items.groomingNotes: Clear extraction item. cmd_diagnose is 56 lines (confirmed lines 5822-5877). Steps are mechanical: move function to lib/cmd-diagnose.sh, delete from main, update dispatch. AC is testable. Good first extraction to validate the lazy-load pattern.

items.title: Extract cmd-groom entry to module
items.intent: Extract only cmd_groom (33 lines) and print_groom_summary (13 lines) — all groom helpers MUST stay in core because sprint loop auto-groom calls them directly
steps: Create .aishore/lib/cmd-groom.sh with cmd_groom and print_groom_summary only
Remove both from main script and update dispatch
Verify run_groom_flow, protect_items_from_groom, enforce_groom_limits etc remain in core
acceptanceCriteria: aishore auto done --dry-run still shows auto-groom capability
items.groomingNotes: Critical boundary: ONLY cmd_groom (33 lines) and print_groom_summary (13 lines) move to module. All groom engine functions (run_groom_flow, protect_items_from_groom, enforce_groom_limits, auto-groom helpers) must stay in core — they are called directly by sprint loop, not via dispatch. Step 3 explicitly says to verify this. AC covers the auto-groom path via --dry-run. Developer must not accidentally move engine functions.

items.title: Extract cmd-backlog-write to module
items.intent: Extract the three write-heavy backlog commands (add 133, edit 191, populate 96 lines) to lazy-loaded module — read commands (list, show, check, rm, history) stay in core
steps: Create .aishore/lib/cmd-backlog-write.sh with cmd_backlog_add, cmd_backlog_edit, cmd_backlog_populate
Remove all three from main script
Update cmd_backlog() router to _load_module for add, edit, populate subcommands
Verify list, show, check, rm, history still work without loading module
acceptanceCriteria: aishore backlog add --title test --type feat creates item
aishore backlog list works without loading module
items.groomingNotes: Good boundary split. Write commands (add 133, edit 191, populate 96 lines) are the heaviest in cmd_backlog and rarely called in sprint paths. Read commands (list, show, check, rm, history) stay in core and must work without loading module. AC step 4 tests this. Critical: cmd_backlog() becomes a router — only load module for add/edit/populate, everything else falls through to inline code.
